title: Shared rate-limit DB contract: rate_limit_buckets + consume_rate_limit_bucket

sha_binding.verified_source_note: The last non-proof commit on this branch, and the head every CI receipt in this bundle was captured against. It is the merge commit produced by GitHub's Update-branch on PR #1477, which brought the branch level with main at eae9f43b; the only thing main introduced since the previous anchor is UTV2-1699 (lane-maximizer repair, its proof bundle and a readiness-ledger refresh), which touches no file this lane touches and no code this lane's evidence depends on. It supersedes 16c15506, which in turn superseded 97e2d9eb after required verify's executable-wiring check correctly refused a test file reachable from no package script. The substantive commit under this anchor is 4c3a71cf, which lands the two fixes returned by PM review: SQL-comment stripping before the RPC parity scan, and a fail-closed refusal on a pre-existing exact function. merge_sha is null pre-merge as the shared schema-v2 evidence contract requires (CEP-E7); post-merge-lane-close.yml binds it to the real merge commit.

live_schema_parity.workflow: Live Schema Parity / Live Schema Parity
live_schema_parity.verdict: FAIL — 10 unauthorized findings, every one of them "missing_in_actual" for public.rate_limit_buckets and its columns, constraints and indexes.
live_schema_parity.why_not_pass: This gate diffs the repo migration set (expected) against the LIVE PRODUCTION database (actual). It reports objects that the repo declares and production does not yet have. UTV2-1811 creates a new relation and production DDL is not authorized, so the gate is correctly reporting a true difference. It cannot return PASS until the migration is applied to production.
live_schema_parity.not_a_merge_blocker: Precise scope of this failure, stated so it cannot be read as harmless. It does NOT block GitHub's merge button: the four required contexts on main are verify, Executor Result Validation, Merge Gate and P0 Protocol, and Live Schema Parity's own required job "Enforce parity (fail-closed)" (job 99933779832) SKIPPED on this feature-branch ref. It DOES block the sanctioned closeout path: Close Eligibility Preflight fails CEP-E7 on this field and therefore CEP-C1, whose own message is that ops:lane-close would fail after merge. Merging this PR before the migration is applied to production would produce a merged-but-unclosable lane, the ghost-lane failure class this repo has hit before. Apply to production first, let parity go green, then merge and close.
live_schema_parity.precedent_measured: Every prior table-creating migration in this repo already exists in production: public.delivery_kill_switch (20260714120000), public.command_center_game_threads and public.command_center_delivery_mappings (20260803230000) all return non-null from to_regclass in zfzdnfwdarxucxtaojxm, while supabase_migrations.schema_migrations holds 127 rows stopping at version 20260801222906. Production DDL has therefore always preceded parity going green; this lane is not deviating from the established order, it is stopped at it awaiting authorization.

acl_proof.capture_method: CAPTURE METHOD — read directly by the orchestrator from the staging catalog (pg_proc.proacl, pg_class.relacl, has_function_privilege, has_table_privilege) over the applied objects, plus a control object built in the same schema without the REVOKE block and then dropped. This block carries NO CI run or job id and is NOT reproducible from any GitHub Actions artifact: no CI job in this repo can produce it, because schema-roundtrip-hash.ts runs pg_dump --no-acl and the CI scratch Postgres has no anon/authenticated/service_role role to grant to. It is therefore weaker evidence than the four receipted fields and must not be read as a CI receipt. It is included because the ACL condition was required to be proven directly, and a pg_dump-based gate structurally cannot prove it. Re-derivable by re-running the same catalog queries against staging.

control_without_revoke.note: Identical objects created in public without the REVOKE block. Proves the revokes are load-bearing, and that a PUBLIC-only revoke would have left the explicit anon and authenticated ACL entries intact.

reversibility.capture_method: CAPTURE METHOD — fingerprints computed by the orchestrator against staging, INCLUDING relacl and proacl, which the CI drill cannot see. This block carries NO CI run or job id. The ACL-blind equivalent IS receipted: schema_roundtrip_drill, run 33530973221 job 99933739000, which independently proves apply/rollback/reapply convergence on a pg_dump --no-acl basis. Treat this block as the ACL-aware supplement to that receipt, not as a receipt itself.
reversibility.note: Fingerprint covers relname, relacl, relrowsecurity, every column with type and nullability, every constraint definition, every index definition, and the function's proacl and prosrc md5. It includes relacl and proacl, which the CI round-trip drill cannot see because its scratch Postgres has no anon, authenticated or service_role role. Measured on the byte-exact file — see runtime_proof.staging_replay_fidelity.

runtime_proof.caller_supplied_window_boundaries: Assumption this migration does not and cannot enforce: p_window_start and p_window_expires_at are supplied by the caller, not computed inside the function. Correct windowing depends on the API server consistently flooring now to the window boundary before calling. The function defends what it can — it rejects null boundaries and p_limit < 1 with 22023, and the table CHECK requires expires_at > window_start — but a caller that passes inconsistent boundaries would get inconsistent windows. That is an API-side contract, out of scope for this migration, and is named here rather than left implicit.

staging_replay_fidelity.note: Closes a fidelity gap that an earlier revision of this bundle carried. The first staging replay executed a whitespace-normalised copy of the migration held in a scratch table, so pg_proc.prosrc did not match the file and the reported fingerprint (f80c62c8..., later 7c00342a...) was a fingerprint of the copy, not of the migration. The replay recorded here executed the migration text verbatim; pg_proc.prosrc on staging now hashes to exactly the md5 of the bytes between the AS $$ delimiters in the committed file, computed independently from the file on disk. Every fingerprint below is therefore a fingerprint of the shipped migration.

preexisting_object_guards.capture_method: CAPTURE METHOD — executed by the orchestrator against staging xskgrzbteyqdufktjrjx (PostgreSQL 17.6) through read/write SQL, each measurement issued as its own statement. Separate statements are required: two calls to a STABLE catalog-reading expression inside one SELECT share a snapshot and return identical, stale values across an intervening DDL, which silently fakes an 'unchanged' result. No CI job produces these numbers; the byte-exact file is separately exercised by the precondition and schema-roundtrip drills, which do have receipts.

static_proof.comment_stripping_scope: Bounded deliberately. stripSqlComments() blanks line comments, block comments (depth-counted, because PostgreSQL nests them), and skips over single-quoted strings, double-quoted identifiers and dollar-quoted bodies so that a `--` inside a function body or a `/*` inside a literal is not mistaken for a comment. It is not a SQL parser and does not attempt to be one; the fixture set includes each of those four shapes, and the CREATE FUNCTION regex then runs over executable text only.

production_migration_ledger.method: supabase migration list --linked could not be run: SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN is empty in local.env and the project is not linked in this checkout, so there is no credential for the CLI's remote read. The remote side was read instead from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations in production over a read-only SELECT — the same table the CLI reads to build its Remote column. production_migration_ledger.intended_command: supabase db push --linked   (equivalently: supabase db push --project-ref zfzdnfwdarxucxtaojxm)
production_migration_ledger.local_only_set: all 8 local versions — none of them appears in the remote ledger
production_migration_ledger.remote_only_set: all 127 remote versions — none of them matches a local filename version

why.mechanism: supabase db push keys on the version prefix of the filename against schema_migrations.version. A local file whose version string is absent from that column is pending.
why.measured: A left join of the 8 local versions against the remote table returned present_in_remote_ledger = false for every one, including 20260801220000_utv2_1640, whose work is demonstrably already in production.
why.root_cause_visible_in_the_data: The remote ledger was not written by pushing these files. Five of the seven pre-existing migrations appear remotely under regenerated version numbers — local 20260714120000 is remote version 20260714203644 under name '20260714120000_add_delivery_kill_switch'; local 20260731000000 is remote version 20260801134241 under name 'utv2_1399_fixture_excluding_reporting_views'; local 20260801000000 is remote 20260801134256; local 20260801220000 is remote 20260801222906. The name column is itself inconsistent, sometimes carrying the local version prefix and sometimes not. Two local migrations have no remote row under any version or name at all: 00000000000000_baseline_live_schema and 20260803230000_utv2_1540_command_center_ledger_repair — although the latter's two tables, command_center_game_threads and command_center_delivery_mappings, do resolve in production. The ledger and the live schema disagree.
why.consequence: A push today would attempt to re-run the full baseline schema and six already-applied migrations against a database that already holds their objects. It would not be a no-op and it would not stop at UTV2-1811.
